entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jan Borman II (unknown–1600) was a Flemish sculptor who played a pivotal role in the Northern Renaissance art movement.

He trained under the renowned Pieter van Aelst, honing his craft in Antwerp before establishing himself as a leading figure in the city's thriving artistic community. His works showcase a unique blend of traditional techniques and innovative, humanist ideals that reflected the values of the emerging middle class.

Borman's sculptures often depicted scenes from classical mythology, biblical narratives, and everyday life, offering a window into the social and cultural norms of 16th-century Flanders.

His art also reflects his strong connection to the Catholic Church, with many of his works featuring intricate carvings and symbolism that underscored the spiritual significance of his creations.

Today, Borman's legacy can be seen in the many museums and galleries across Europe where his masterpieces are admired by scholars and enthusiasts alike.

As a testament to his enduring influence, 'The Virgin and Child with St. John the Baptist,' one of Borman's most celebrated works, is now considered an iconic representation of Flemish Renaissance art.
